title: Rollup tiers: each built from the one below, each kept for longer
caption: The query layer picks the coarsest tier that still gives ~1,000 points for the range.

steps.text: Minute buckets come from the raw stream. Raw events are kept only long enough to replay a week.
An hour row merges its 60 minute rows; a day row merges 24 hour rows. No tier goes back to raw events, which only works if the stored values are mergeable.
A "last 24 h" panel reads 1,440 minute rows; "last 30 days" reads 720 hour rows; "last 2 years" reads 730 day rows.

scenarios.name: Backfill after a bug
scenarios.summary: A bug overcounted for 3 days: replay the raw log through the fixed job, then re-merge hours and days. Anything older than raw retention can no longer be fixed.

steps.text: A deploy double-counts mobile clicks; three days of minute rows are wrong.
Hour and day rows were merged from those minutes, so they're wrong too.
Re-run the fixed job over the raw log for those days and overwrite the minute rows.
Re-merge the affected hour and day rows from the corrected minutes.
Had the bug lasted 10 days, the first 3 would stay wrong: the raw retention is your repair window.

scenarios.name: New dimension
scenarios.summary: 'Clicks by country' needs new rollups in every tier, and they can be backfilled only as far back as raw events are kept, so the new panel starts with a week of history.

steps.text: The existing tiers are keyed by (ad, bucket); country isn't in them and can't be recovered from them.
Add country to the stream job's key and backfill from the raw log: only 7 days exist.
Hour and day rows by country build up from there, going forward.
The query layer must say 'by-country data starts on <date>' for longer ranges.

scenarios.name: Alternative: one tier
scenarios.summary: Keep only minute rows, forever: simpler to build, but a 2-year panel reads ~1M rows per series and the table grows by ~43k rows per series every month.

steps.text: The stream job writes minute rows, and nothing ever merges or deletes them.
'Last 2 years' reads about 1M rows per series for a chart that can show ~1,000 points: the panel times out.
